minutes.headline: Parks Commission held off deciding the skate park bond amount, deferring to Chris Ruth's review first
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission discussed repeated vandalism and a proposed noise-deterrent device at Wallace Park, then spent most of the meeting on the Marshall Park skate park project: whether to require a costly completion bond or a much cheaper restorative bond, and concerns that the master plan's new park location will change once construction begins. No formal vote was taken; the board agreed to let Anthony consult town staff on a bond figure and reconvene, likely by Zoom, to finalize the contract.

budget_items.topic: Mosquito anti-loitering deterrent for Wallace Park
budget_items.what_was_said: A noise device that only younger people can hear was proposed to discourage loitering/vandalism at Wallace Park after repeated playground damage. A rough cost was floated as not being unreasonable.

Chris Ruth is preparing a capital plan submission for the fields to send to the finance committee, hoping it meets an unspecified funding threshold; he is unsure how much capital funding will be allotted this year.

budget_items.topic: Skate park project cost and fundraising
budget_items.what_was_said: The builder's cost on paper plus donated materials were described, with a running total and amount raised so far given.

budget_items.topic: Skate park completion bond estimate (worst case)
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager's analysis, described as a worst-case scenario, put the cost to finish the park if the town had to complete it, and bonding capacity was limited by what an unlicensed group could be bonded for.
figures_as_heard: a million and a half dollars

budget_items.topic: Restorative bond vs. completion bond cost comparison
budget_items.what_was_said: A restorative bond (to return the site to its prior state if the project fails) was quoted as far cheaper than a completion bond, with quotes gathered from several contractors for site removal and restoration.
The commission discussed settling on a bond amount to request, weighing whether to ask for a lower or higher figure, deferring to Chris Ruth's estimate.

decisions.decision: Chair to send board members a link about the mosquito anti-loitering device for feedback to give to Chris Ruth.
A board member will print and laminate 'park closed dusk to dawn' signage herself rather than wait on an order through Chris.

Approval of the skate park contract's bond terms made conditional on Anthony confirming a restorative-bond figure (around $100,000) with Chris Ruth; if he disagrees, a further meeting will be scheduled.
If Chris Ruth's feedback is acceptable, the board will hold a short Zoom meeting to vote on and execute the contract rather than wait for the next regular meeting.
The right-of-entry agreement's new expiration/entry date will be set roughly a year out (around October of next year or August 1 as a cushion) rather than reusing the prior July date.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission took no vote on the skate park bond, holding off until Anthony confirms a restorative-bond figure with town staff.
The board plans a short Zoom meeting to vote on and sign the skate park contract once that figure comes back, rather than waiting for its next regular meeting.
Repeated vandalism at Wallace Park's playground led to discussion of a noise-based deterrent device and hand-made signage, with no cost approved.
A member raised unresolved concern that the master plan's planned park location may shift once skate park construction begins at Marshall Park.

why_it_matters: The bond type the town requires for the skate park sets how much financial exposure the town carries if the project is not finished.
The contract vote is expected to happen at a short Zoom session rather than a regular posted meeting, which changes how residents can follow or weigh in.
